Hi Alex —

Great to meet earlier today. Quick recap and the MAP milestone to get the load/performance test scheduled:

Goal: Replay a representative slice of Acme production traffic to validate latency and throughput on Redwood Dedicated (or Hosted with burst) and confirm capacity sizing before pilot.

Proposed MAP milestone: 
- Milestone: Load/perf test scheduling and execution
- Target close date: 2026-03-12
- Responsibilities:
  - Acme: provide anonymized production request trace (CSV/JSON), peak QPS window, and SRE point-of-contact for network/quota work.
  - Redwood: prepare test harness (traffic replay tooling), estimate dedicated capacity sizing, run tests, and deliver results summary + recommended capacity.
- Dependencies: production trace + endpoint mapping from Acme; test window (2 half-days preferred); test credentials and any allowlists for IPs.

Proposed test windows (pick 1):
- Wed, Feb 25 (PST) — 10:00–14:00 PT
- Thu, Feb 26 (PST) — 08:00–12:00 PT

Notes / ask for this reply: could you confirm peak QPS, which endpoints to include (NLP inference vs batch embeddings), and SRE contact to coordinate network/config? I attached a draft MAP for your review (redwood_map_draft_v1.xlsx).

If those windows don't work we can shift; want to lock this milestone into the MAP so it doesn't slip.

Thanks —
Marissa
Director, Strategic Accounts

Thanks for the recap and MAP draft, that looks good. Quick answers:
- Peak QPS: our production peak for the inference endpoints is ~420 QPS sustained for a 45-minute window; 800 QPS short burst observed for spikes (1–2 min).
- Endpoints to include: real-time text-gen endpoint (primary), and batch embeddings for analytics (secondary).
- SRE contact: sre-team@acme-corp.com (I'll loop them in separately if needed).

Windows: Feb 25 works for us (10:00–14:00 PT). Can Redwood confirm whether we should run against Redwood Dedicated or Hosted? We will prefer Dedicated sizing guidance if possible — our procurement lead will need that for the Reserved Capacity conversation.

We can share a sanitized production trace and endpoint mapping by EOD Friday (Feb 20). Let me know what format you prefer for the trace.

Appreciate it —

Hi Alex / Marissa —

Thanks for the numbers, Alex — very helpful. Quick technical note and request so we can size properly:

What we need from Acme (preferred formats):
- Traffic trace: per-request timestamp, endpoint path, payload size (tokens), and response size. JSONL or CSV is fine.
- Breakdown of QPS by endpoint if possible (e.g., text-gen: 350 sustained / 800 burst; embeddings: 70 sustained).
- Any auth/allowlist config that could affect peak connections.

Preliminary sizing (ballpark) given 420 sustained / 800 burst for primary text-gen:
- Dedicated estimate: 4 x A100-equivalent GPUs for sustained SLA with headroom (depends on prompt lengths and model variant); we can run a test on Hosted with a scaled cluster first to validate.
- If you want full redundancy and <100ms p50 on primary endpoint at peak, we may recommend 6 GPUs in Dedicated for production.

Proposed test plan:
1) Feb 25 — morning: run traffic replay on Hosted (replicate traffic shapes) to baseline performance and identify hotspots.
2) Feb 25 — afternoon: replay on a Dedicated-like cluster (we'll provision a temporary cluster matching the 4-GPU spec) to validate capacity.
3) Feb 26 (fallback): rerun with tuned batching/kv-cache settings if needed.

I'll attach a short runbook with traffic-replay steps and the data format we need (aditya_traffic_replay_steps.md). Can you share the sanitized trace by Feb 20 EOD so we can prepare? Also confirm whether you need Redwood to propose a Reserved Capacity quote — we can include a sizing estimate in the MAP milestone deliverable.

Thanks —
Aditya
Principal Performance Engineer
Redwood Inference
